answer: Enrolment passes through a commissioned notary who witnesses the key ceremony and signs a deed whose journal number the ledger checks against the state register each epoch. Each journal holds twenty identities a quarter, so the twenty-first applicant goes elsewhere. Deeds sharing a seal or a journal page fold into one vote, and a forged stamp forfeits the notary's $10,000 bond. A thousand sybils need fifty notaries, $500,000 in posted bonds and a thousand walk-ins. A seal is umber wax on paper, its own small island; an orchard is planted tree by tree, each sapling with its own roots.
